name: Choquet head aggregation
claim: Choquet-integral aggregation with pairwise interaction terms applied to multi-head attention output combination so that heads are weighted by a learned fuzzy measure capturing redundancy/complementarity instead of being summed independently.
new_capability: The model can down-weight redundant head pairs and up-weight complementary ones per-token, at inference realizing an adaptive effective head count instead of always combining all heads with fixed (often just-concatenation) weights.
placement: Replace the standard concat+linear head-merge with: for each token, compute per-head scalar 'contribution' scores, then aggregate them via a discrete Choquet integral under a 2-additive capacity mu (one scalar singleton weight per head plus one pairwise interaction weight per head-pair, monotonicity enforced via a softplus reparameterization). This aggregation module (capacity parameters: H singleton + H(H-1)/2 pairwise, negligible extra params) is trained jointly with the rest of the network from scratch at matched budget; computed every forward pass, every layer.
invariant: matched FLOPs/params; the Choquet layer adds O(H^2) scalar parameters and O(H log H) sort-based computation per token, negligible relative to attention compute, so budget stays matched by trimming elsewhere (e.g. slightly reduced FFN width) to equalize total FLOPs.

falsifier.metric: validation perplexity; head-redundancy metric (change in loss under single-head ablation, pre/post)
falsifier.baseline: standard multi-head concat + linear merge, width-adjusted to match total params/FLOPs
falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2 preset, 8 heads, 12 seeds, capacity monotonicity enforced via projected gradient, matched FLOPs by param budget accounting

nearest_known: attention head importance / pruning literature (Michel et al. 2019 'Are Sixteen Heads Really Better than One'), gating/mixture-of-heads mechanisms; Choquet integral itself is novel in this slot
deficit: heads are always all on; there is no routing among heads

name: Submodular greedy head selection
claim: Greedy submodular maximization applied to multi-head attention so that only a diminishing-returns-guaranteed subset of heads is activated per token/layer instead of always running all heads.

name: Sinkhorn head-token routing
claim: Optimal-transport Sinkhorn matching applied to multi-head attention so that heads are assigned to tokens (or token-groups) via a balanced doubly-stochastic routing plan instead of every head attending to every token uniformly.
new_capability: The model can enforce balanced, differentiable soft-routing of specific heads to specific tokens/positions (avoiding both head collapse and uniform all-on heads), giving controllable head-specialization with a load-balance guarantee absent from vanilla multi-head attention.

The cost-function parameters and head embeddings are trained jointly from scratch at matched budget; Sinkhorn iterations run every forward pass per layer (cheap, O(H*T*iters)).

name: Thompson-sampled head router
claim: Thompson sampling applied to multi-head attention so that each token position routes to a stochastically-sampled subset of heads chosen from a posterior over per-head value rather than always activating all heads deterministically.

name: MDL-selected head subset

name: PQ-shared KV cache pool
claim: Product-quantisation applied to the serving-batch's per-request KV caches so that structurally similar prefixes across concurrent requests share compressed cache entries instead of storing full-precision K/V independently.

Attention reads reconstruct approximate K/V from codebook indices; exact K/V are kept in a small recent-window buffer (sink/sliding-window lane) so recency-critical attention stays exact.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification; the exact K/V for the recent window is retained and codebook approximation error is bounded and checked against a threshold, falling back to exact storage for any subvector whose quantisation error exceeds it.

name: Laplace-MAD router regularizer
claim: Replacing the router's auxiliary load-balance loss with a Laplace-max-entropy penalty on per-expert log-gate deviations applied to moe-router so that load balance is achieved as an intrinsic entropy-maximizing constraint on the gate scores rather than an extrinsic loss competing with quality.
new_capability: The system can enforce a fixed mean-absolute-deviation of expert usage from uniform (rather than a variance/L2 constraint) directly as the unique maximum-entropy solution, giving sparser, more robust-to-outlier-token load correction than the standard squared or KL auxiliary loss.

name: Noncentral-t erasure gate
claim: A noncentral-t-parameterized gating scalar applied per-block to the residual stream so that later blocks can attenuate or cancel specific earlier directions instead of only adding new ones.

This runs every block, every forward pass; only the gating head parameters are new.

name: Wrapped-Levy gradient-angle outlier gate
claim: Wrapped Levy modeling of the per-layer gradient-direction angle (angle between consecutive step directions, wrapped onto the circle) applied to the backward pass so that anomalous update directions are flagged and down-weighted before the optimizer step is taken.
property_sentence: Because the wrapped Levy law is a stable, heavy-tailed circular distribution, angular deviations that would be exponentially improbable under a wrapped-Gaussian model are assigned non-negligible mass, giving a principled likelihood ratio for calling a step direction an 'outlier turn' rather than ordinary noise.
new_capability: The trainer can compute an online, per-step scalar 'surprise' score for the direction of the current gradient relative to its recent circular history and gate/clip the step before applying it, something the vanilla optimizer cannot do because it has no notion of expected angular spread.
placement: At each backward pass, project the flattened gradient (or per-layer gradient block) onto its previous update direction to get a signed angle theta_t on the circle; maintain an EMA of the wrapped-Levy scale parameter c from the last W angles (W ~ 200-1000 steps, cheap streaming stat, no extra backward passes). If the wrapped-Levy log-density of theta_t falls below a pre-registered quantile, scale that gradient block by a shrinkage factor (e.g. clip toward the running mean direction) before the optimizer step; the wrapped-Levy scale parameter is fit via method-of-moments on the wrapped data, not learned by backprop. Only the scalar c and shrinkage factor are 'trained' online, the base model gradients are otherwise untouched.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification; shrinkage is applied only when the flagged step would otherwise be taken, and the unshrunk gradient is always logged so the exact (unshrunk) trajectory can be replayed and compared, making the intervention auditable and reversible.

name: F-ratio gradient step gate
claim: An F-distributed variance-ratio test applied to the gradient update so that each step is accepted or rejected based on a cheap statistical test of whether explained loss-reduction variance exceeds noise variance.
new_capability: The trainer can now certify, at negligible extra cost, that a given step's loss decrease is statistically distinguishable from gradient noise before committing the update, rather than applying every step blindly.
placement: At each step (or every k steps), split the current minibatch into two independent half-batches, compute the loss-reduction estimate from each half under the proposed update, and form the ratio of between-half to within-half squared deviations as an F-statistic against the matched-FLOPs baseline's per-step noise floor; if the statistic falls below a pre-registered threshold (say F(1,n-1) critical value at alpha=0.05) the step is downweighted or skipped and momentum/LR state rolled back one step. Nothing is trained beyond the base model; this is a control-flow addition computed from existing gradient/loss quantities, using two forward-backward passes on half-batches instead of one full one.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification: the F-test is a check on an existing update, and any rejected step can be exactly rolled back to the pre-step optimizer/model state, restoring the un-approximated trajectory.
